title: Creative sets up to computable permutation

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §17.1 Lemma 17.1 and its full proof, p.71, specialized to ordinary computability; §5.2 Theorem 5.7, p.30, used through the preceding Myhill entry

summary: Turn halting reductions into injective reductions by self-reference, then classify creative sets up to computable permutation.
abstract: A creative set can encode every computably enumerable membership problem, but the encoding may send different inputs to the same number. To obtain a computable permutation, we first make a halting reduction injective. Two self-referential programs provide the key step: one copies an old computation if its image is fresh; if its image collides with a finite record, a second program is forced to escape. Iterating this step supplies arbitrarily many equivalent halting queries with distinct images. A finite scan then chooses a new output at each input. Combined with injective halting completeness and Myhill’s finite-matching construction, this shows that the creative sets are exactly the computable permutations of the halting set. The construction gives both a permutation and its computable inverse.
